# Code and reproduction notes

Study: how much shorter can a prediction-powered confidence interval for E[Y] be when the labeled set, the unlabeled set
and the predictor are fixed? (Delivered under `code/` and `results/` of the paper repository; the same files are in
`experiment-repo`.) Result files: `results/README.md` (what each was computed on) and `results/METHODS.md` (definitions of
every method id, interval construction and column).

## Layout
```
src/pci/          library: calibrators.py (g(Z) fits), estimators.py (pooled cross-fitted estimator, PPI/PPI++ via ppi-python,
                  intervals, 1-SE selection), pops.py (real pools, synthetic generators with known truth, floor statistics,
                  shift / non-MCAR / rare-event populations), runner.py (Monte-Carlo driver, resumable cells), analysis.py, paths.py
experiments/      one script per experiment (E1..E7), floors*.py, nstar_ci.py, ballots_native.py, get_data.py
analysis/         build_results.py (all delivered tables), finite_pop_check.py (disjoint-draw cells vs finite-population prediction), planned.py (planned vs stored cells), sync_delivery.sh
results/          aggregated CSV/JSON/MD (delivered); results/exp*/ raw per-replicate cells (*.npz, not in git; release asset)
```
`results/` is found automatically (`$PCI_RESULTS`, else `<root>/results`, else `<root>/../results`); data in `$PCI_DATA`
(default `/hutian/work/data`).

## Environment
Python 3.11.2; numpy 2.4.6, scipy 1.17.1, pandas 3.0.6, scikit-learn 1.9.1, **ppi-python 0.2.3** (PPI / PPI++ baselines), gdown 6.5.2
(see `requirements.txt`). CPU only. All worker processes are single-threaded (`OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`, set in `experiments/common.py`).

## Data
Nine example sets of `ppi-python==0.2.3` (loader `ppi_py.datasets.load_dataset`, anonymous Google Drive download via `gdown`):
`python experiments/get_data.py` downloads whatever is missing into `$PCI_DATA` and writes `results/data_sha256.txt`
(SHA-256 and array shapes of the files used). Nothing else is downloaded; no model is trained (the supplied `Yhat` is the fixed predictor).

## Seeds
Cell seed = 20261126 + crc32(cell id) mod 10^6 (`experiments/common.py`); replicate r uses `numpy.random.SeedSequence([seed, r])`,
so a cell is reproducible and independent of the number of processes. Bootstrap indices in `analysis/build_results.py` use fixed seeds (0, 1).
Every stored cell records its seed, its replicate count and the code version (git SHA, `+dirty` if the working tree differed) in its meta data.
The estimator code (`src/pci/{calibrators,estimators,pops,runner,analysis}.py`) is unchanged since commit 931cb22, which fixed the arms; later commits add
scripts, `paths.py` and analysis only (`git diff 931cb22 HEAD -- src experiments`).

# Review of Version 1 (paper-repo#9, head 7ef2dac, document built from 7ef2dac28951)

Read: `main/document.pdf` (24 pp; main text 8 pp, refs from p. 9) from page 1; code/results of the head
(`results/headline.csv`, `results/cells.csv`, `code/README.md`) for the numbers I could check.

## What the paper claims and whether it holds
With n, N and f fixed, PPI++ is within ~1% of the width of any interval built from the same labels on nine
real datasets (reference n); room exists where E[Y|f] is far from affine; the one real gain over the package
(gene_expression, n=100) is the package's clip of lambda. Exact gap (1/n-1/M)*Delta and a break-even n*.

Checks against the results: Prop. 1 / eq. (3), (5) re-derived by hand: correct. Headline ratios at the reference
n (0.994..1.008 vs strongest valid baseline; 0.971..1.007 vs package; gene_expression r=0.971), 51 T1 cells
(38/12/1 vs package, 39/12/0 vs strongest valid) and the Table 1 validity marks all reproduce from
`headline.csv` / `cells.csv`. The pre-fixed rule and its post-hoc strengthening are both reported as such.
The claims are supported and appropriately scoped (negative / conditional result, accepted by the task).

## Findings
- **must M1 (consistency).** Abstract says "a label saving of at most 1.1%", Introduction ("What we find") says
  "label saving at most 1.2%". `headline.csv` gives 1 - 0.9943^2 = 1.13% (gene_expression) -> 1.1%. Make the
  introduction (and any other place) say the same, derived from the unrounded ratio.
- **must M2 (unexplained notation in the main text).** "A6", "B5" (Table 1 headers, Fig. 1 axis labels), the
  "base class" column with entries P / U (Table 1), and the panel title "C1: excess over floor" (Fig. 2) are
  internal identifiers (arm / claim numbers) that the main text never defines; a reader outside the study
  cannot decode them. Use the names the text uses ("selected T1 interval", "selected T1+X interval"), define
  P/U in the caption (package / unclipped) or drop the column, and drop the "C1" panel title.
  (Venue record also asks for no titles inside graphics.)
- may M3 (readability). Section 6 is a dense sequence of paragraphs each carrying 8-15 numbers and a caveat;
  "the reading against the strongest valid baseline was fixed after the first results" appears in Sec. 4, the
  Introduction/abstract and Sec. 7. Say it once in Sec. 4 and keep the Results to what each exhibit shows.
  The abstract carries ~15 numbers; a reader outside the study would take the first four sentences and the
  conclusion better with fewer.
- may M4 (validity rule). The rule "Wilson upper < 0.95" marks PPI++ invalid at 94.36% coverage with 5000
  repetitions (alphafold, n=500) and puts 57 of 113 cells in Fig. 3 as "all fail"; with no multiplicity
  correction and a one-sided rule this over-labels near-nominal cells. A sensitivity line (e.g. tolerance 0.94)
  would show the headline classification does not depend on it.
- may M5 (baselines). Fisch et al.'s stratified PPI is named as the closest relative but not run as published;
  the post-hoc `strat_ppi` arm (stratum means of f, in the estimator class) is. Say in one sentence that the
  strata-means class covers it.
- may M6 (break-even test). The scoring tolerance (factor 3, fixed in advance) is generous; the paper states
  it and reports the miss on gene_expression and census_income-log, so it is a statement of what was tested,
  not a defect.

## Strongest objections a reviewer would raise and what answers each
1. *Novelty / ICML significance.* The floor, cross-fitting and AIPW are classical; the contribution is the
